summary: Iran claims a new strike on a US base in Bahrain, Zelenskyy says the US floated Donbas-for-NATO, COP31 stalls on fossil fuels, and SpaceX catches a ship from orbit.

question.text: Several stories today rest on one side's account: Iran's strike claims, Zelenskyy's report of a US offer, an army's battlefield gains. When only one party has described an event, what would you need to see before treating it as what happened?

read.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting at APEC: What to expect
read.summary: Why the three leaders are meeting in Shenzhen, what each wants on nuclear arms, Iran and trade, and why Ukraine is officially off the agenda.

topics.heading: Iran claims a second drone strike on a US radar in Bahrain; tankers hit mines near Hormuz
topics.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones targeted a US radar at a base in Bahrain on Sunday, their second such claim in three days; Bahrain says its defences stopped several attacks.[^1] Iran's navy also says tankers using unapproved routes hit mines near the Strait of Hormuz.[^3]

lead.title: Iran says it targets US radar in Bahrain. What do we know?

alsoReported.title: Iran says 2 oil tankers hit sea mines, catch fire near Strait of Hormuz
Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain, and other Mideast news

article: Early on Sunday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said six drones had attacked a US air-defence radar at Riffa Air Base in Bahrain, which they called retaliation for "hostile" US actions.[^1][^2] Bahrain's Interior Ministry sent two alerts within about three hours telling residents to go to the nearest safe place, and the Bahrain Defence Force said its air defences stopped several Iranian "aerial attacks".[^1] The US military had not commented on Sunday's claim when Al Jazeera published.[^1]

It is the second claim in three days. On Friday the IRGC said it had "destroyed" a US early-warning radar in Bahrain; US Central Command said it shot down two drones and that there was no damage or injury.[^4][^1] Bahrain matters because it hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, and the war that began on Feb 28 has already damaged US sites in eight countries, according to a Pentagon inspector general report cited by Al Jazeera.[^1]

At sea, the IRGC navy says two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday after using an unauthorised route with their tracking signals off, and Iran's regular navy reported a third.[^3][^2] No ships, crews or casualties have been named, and none of this has been independently confirmed. The US says it has cleared the main shipping lanes of mines and is keeping its blockade of Iranian ports.[^3]

Diplomacy has not stopped. Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says Tehran sent seven conditions through a Qatari mediator, including lifting the blockade and sanctions and formally ending the war, and is waiting for a US reply.[^1] Separately, a confidential report from the UN nuclear watchdog (IAEA) says it does not know the exact location of a new Iranian enrichment plant or whether it holds nuclear material, which it calls a serious concern.[^5]
My read: both sides are signalling without committing. Small incidents with competing accounts are where a slow standoff could turn into wider fighting, so the next US response matters.
topics.differences: The IRGC says Friday's strike destroyed a US radar; US Central Command says it downed both drones with no damage.[^4] For Sunday, Iran claims an attack on the radar while Bahrain says it repelled several attacks; the US had not commented.[^1] Iran says tankers hit mines on unauthorised routes; the US says the main lanes are clear.[^3]

topics.heading: Zelenskyy says US envoys floated Donbas-for-NATO; Trump, Xi and Putin meet Thursday
topics.summary: Ukraine's president says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, the first time he says the two were linked.[^6] The White House says Trump, Xi and Putin will meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, without Ukraine on the agenda.[^8]

lead.title: US floated idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskiy says

alsoReported.title: Zelenskyy questions SpaceX over reported Starshield speed restrictions
Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of APEC, White House says

article: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters that US negotiators had asked, in effect, "What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?"[^6] Donbas is the industrial region in eastern Ukraine that Russia demands in full and partly occupies. Zelenskyy said Kyiv is not ready to give up territory, but that if a full package of security guarantees, a well-funded army and rebuilding money were offered, he would put the question to a referendum because "I have no right to make that decision on my own."[^6][^7]

The idea, if it is real, runs into an old obstacle: Russian President Vladimir Putin has long called Ukrainian NATO membership a red line.[^6] The latest US-brokered round in Abu Dhabi ended with agreement on a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people, with final numbers still being worked out. US envoy Jared Kushner said both sides had taken "maximalist positions", and Zelenskyy said Putin personally does not support a ceasefire.[^6]

Europe has chosen a five-country team (the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, plus EU institutions) for the next round, expected in Abu Dhabi; the Kremlin says Europe must first show it is ready to help.[^9] Meanwhile the White House says Presidents Trump, Xi and Putin will meet on Thursday in Shenzhen, at the APEC summit, to discuss the Iran war and nuclear arms limits. A senior US official said Trump will not raise Ukraine and that no agreements are expected.[^8][^27]

Zelenskyy also says SpaceX's military Starlink service, Starshield, has been capping Ukrainian terminals in occupied areas at 161 km/h for five days, which hampers drones used to intercept Russian jet drones. He said Ukraine does not believe SpaceX's explanation of a technical issue and has asked the State Department, Pentagon and SpaceX to explain.[^7]
What to watch: whether Washington confirms or denies the Donbas-for-NATO idea, and whether Ukraine comes up in Shenzhen despite US assurances.
topics.differences: Zelenskyy's account of the US proposal has not been confirmed by Washington in these reports.[^6] US officials say Ukraine is not on the Shenzhen agenda; Zelenskyy has worried a deal could be discussed without Kyiv, and the Kremlin rejects comparisons with the 1945 Yalta conference.[^8]

topics.heading: Israel kills a Hamas commander in a Gaza tent camp; 18 countries condemn a hospital strike
topics.summary: Israel says it killed Samir Abu Younis, head of Hamas's Rafah brigade, in a strike on a tent camp in al-Mawasi; Gaza's health ministry reports 16 people killed in 48 hours.[^10][^11] Foreign ministers of 18 countries condemned an earlier strike near Nasser Hospital.[^12]

lead.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza

alsoReported.title: Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say
Several muslim countries condemn IDF's strike on Gaza hospital, call for lifting aid restrictions

article: Israel's military and the Shin Bet security service say they killed Samir Abu Younis, 53, who had led Hamas's Rafah brigade since September, in a strike on Saturday in the al-Mawasi area of southern Gaza.[^11] Witnesses told the BBC that missiles hit a tent in a camp for displaced people. Israel says it took steps to reduce harm to civilians; Hamas's armed wing called it a "cowardly assassination".[^11][^10]

The strike came during a ceasefire that has held since October 2025, but only loosely. Israel says the truce terms allow it to strike remaining militants.[^11] Gaza's health ministry, which is run by Hamas, says 16 people were killed and 68 injured in the past 48 hours, and that at least 1,643 have died since the ceasefire began; AP puts that figure at more than 1,600.[^10] Al Jazeera reports 11 deaths from cold, including a nine-month-old baby.[^10]

On Friday, foreign ministers of 18 mostly Muslim-majority countries, including Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey and Indonesia, condemned an earlier Israeli strike near Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, which the health ministry says killed six. Israel says it targeted a Hamas brigade commander. The ministers also called for limits on aid to be lifted; the UN estimates about 1.4 million Gazans live in tents, while Israel says it has let in 93,000 tents.[^12]

In Israel, politics will shape what comes next. Gadi Eisenkot, who has the first chance to form a government after the election, is reported to be prioritising talks with the ultra-Orthodox parties, who want limits on military service for religious students.[^13] My read: until a government is formed, the stuck second phase of the Gaza plan (disarmament, foreign troops, rebuilding) is unlikely to move.
topics.differences: Israel describes the al-Mawasi strike as a targeted killing permitted by the truce;[^11] Hamas calls it an assassination, and 18 governments condemned the hospital strike as a violation.[^12] Casualty figures come from Gaza's health ministry and differ slightly between outlets.[^10]

topics.heading: COP31's first week ends deadlocked on fossil fuels as a first draft deal is promised
topics.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended its first week with no agreement on moving away from fossil fuels; UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators to avoid "tactical delays".[^14] A first draft of the deal text is expected early this week.[^14]

lead.title: UN climate chief urges faster action at COP31

alsoReported.title: COP31 First Week Ends Deadlocked on Fossil Fuels as UN Climate Chief Urges Swift Deal
UN talks enter decisive phase amid deep divisions over climate resilience

article: Negotiators at COP31, the yearly UN climate conference, finished their first week on Saturday without agreeing how to word a move away from coal, oil and gas.[^15] Simon Stiell, the UN's climate chief, told countries to "avoid tactical delays", saying agreement on "every word, every sentence is tough but vital work."[^14] Australia's Chris Bowen, who is helping lead the talks, said a first draft of the deal should arrive early this week.[^14]

The Turkish hosts have put forward a "summary of options" on fossil fuels, forests, oceans and how to handle overshooting the 1.5C warming limit.[^15] Their headline idea is to raise electricity's share of the world's energy use to 35% by 2035, from a little over one-fifth today. Some delegations were disappointed that the extra power would not have to come from renewables.[^14][^15]

The split is familiar. The EU, UK, Japan and Canada want the deal tied closely to the Global Stocktake, the UN's review of how far countries are off track. India, China and the Arab and African groups insist each country sets its own path and that rich countries pay more; Saudi Arabia and Russia have long resisted limits on fossil fuels.[^16][^14] Campaigners say a promised mechanism to help workers through the transition has been watered down, and no new money has been pledged to the fund for climate loss and damage.[^16] The US is skipping the talks for a second year.[^15]

Tens of thousands of people marched in Antalya on Saturday.[^16] My read: the key test this week is whether the draft text names fossil fuels at all. A UN report last month found the world is on course to pass 1.5C, so even a strong deal would mostly be about how far above it warming goes.[^14]
topics.differences: Rich-country blocs want firmer collective goals tied to the Global Stocktake; India, China and the Arab and African groups want national choice plus more finance.[^16] Greenpeace says the host's options are not binding and need strengthening, while the UK and European leaders back the electrification target.[^15]

topics.heading: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage with its launch tower for the first time
topics.summary: After a 22.5-hour orbital test flight, SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft with the arms of its launch tower in Texas, a first for a vehicle returning from orbit; the booster's catch attempt failed.[^17][^18]

lead.title: SpaceX makes history as Starship spacecraft caught by launch tower for first time

alsoReported.title: Starship Flight 15 Ends With First Ship Tower Catch
Starship Flight 15: Ship 42 caught by the tower

article: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launched from Starbase, Texas, on Friday evening and spent about 22.5 hours in orbit, its longest flight so far, before the ship returned on Saturday and was caught in mid-air by the giant mechanical arms on its launch tower.[^19][^18] It is the first time an upper stage coming back from orbit has been caught this way.[^18] During the flight, the ship released 26 Starlink internet satellites.[^17][^19]

Why it matters: almost every rocket's upper stage is thrown away after one use, which is a large part of why spaceflight is expensive. SpaceX had already caught its Super Heavy first-stage boosters three times; catching the ship as well is a key step towards a rocket that is fully reusable, like an airliner.[^17] A SpaceX commentator called it "the holy grail of spaceflight", and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called it "almost magic".[^18][^17]

Not everything worked. The booster did not make its own catch and ended up in the Gulf of Mexico. Accounts differ on the details: Fox Business reports its engines shut down early and it exploded over the water, while drohnen.de cites a guidance problem and Elon Musk saying it was slightly low on fuel.[^17][^19]

NASA's Artemis plan to return astronauts to the Moon depends on Starship, so each test is also watched as a measure of that schedule.[^17] My read: one catch is a proof of concept, not a routine. The real test is whether SpaceX can catch, refuel and refly ships quickly and cheaply, which has not yet been shown.
topics.differences: Sources describe the booster's failure differently: an early engine shutdown and explosion (Fox Business) or an aborted catch and splashdown after a guidance issue (drohnen.de).[^17][^19]

topics.heading: Sudan's army says it retook al-Khuwai in West Kordofan from the RSF
topics.summary: Sudan's army and allied forces say they recaptured the West Kordofan town of al-Khuwai and nearby villages from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces; the RSF has not responded.[^21][^22]

lead.title: How SAF successes in Sudan's Kordofan could turn tide against the RSF

alsoReported.title: Sudanese army, allies announce recapture of key West Kordofan town
Sudan Army Says It Has Taken Khuwei Town

article: Sudan's army and its allied Joint Force, made up of former Darfur rebel groups, say they took back al-Khuwai and several nearby villages in West Kordofan on Friday.[^21][^22] The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group that has been fighting the army since April 2023, had held the town since May 2025. The Joint Force claims it destroyed 20 RSF vehicles and seized 40; those claims have not been verified, and the RSF had not responded.[^21][^22]

The town sits on roads linking North and West Kordofan with Darfur, the RSF's stronghold in the west. Joint Force leader Minni Minnawi called it "a route towards Umm Dafuq", a town near the borders with Chad and the Central African Republic.[^21] Al Jazeera reports that the army's offensive has already broken the RSF's siege of the city of al-Obeid, though the RSF still holds al-Nuhud and parts of South Kordofan.[^20]

The stakes are large. Al Jazeera cites estimates of about 150,000 people killed and more than 14 million of Sudan's 53 million people displaced, and notes that oilfields in West Kordofan produce about 90% of the country's oil.[^20] The army also says it shot down a drone over Blue Nile state that came from the direction of Ethiopia, a sign of how the war draws in neighbours.[^21]

My read: gains in Kordofan could shift the balance between the two sides, but front lines in this war have moved back and forth before, and neither side has shown it can win outright. Both have been accused of serious abuses against civilians, so who controls a town matters a great deal to the people living there.
topics.differences: The army and Joint Force describe a decisive victory; their figures on RSF losses are unverified and the RSF has not given its account.[^21][^22]

topics.heading: Nvidia reports without its founder as Anthropic's IPO draws heavy demand
topics.summary: Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, its first since Jensen Huang resigned, while Reuters says orders for Anthropic's share sale were about six times the shares on offer.[^25][^23] Together they are a test of confidence in the AI boom.

lead.title: Investors flock to Anthropic IPO but question durability of AI lead

alsoReported.title: Nvidia has crucial week ahead with earnings call and ex-CEO Jensen Huang's spy scandal hearing
Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit

article: Two events this week will be read as a check on the AI boom. On Tuesday, Nvidia, whose chips power most AI systems, reports its quarterly results, its first since founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive on Nov 12 amid a scandal over AI chips reaching China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim CEO. Analysts expect revenue of about $109 billion.[^25]

Huang's exit has rattled governments that rely on Nvidia. South Korea says the company reaffirmed plans to supply 260,000 chips, Singapore is continuing an investigation into a company called Megaspeed, and Taiwan says Nvidia's planned overseas headquarters there is still on track.[^26] US lawmakers want Huang to testify in early December.[^25]

Meanwhile Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude AI models, is selling shares to the public for the first time. Reuters reports that orders were about six times the shares available by Thursday, with pricing expected on Wednesday for an offering of about $64 billion at a price range that would value the company at up to about $1.4 trillion.[^23][^24] Investors interviewed raised doubts too: whether Anthropic can stay ahead as Google catches up, and whether its business can grow beyond coding tools.[^23]
A note on bias: this brief is written with the help of Claude, which is made by Anthropic. I have tried to report the IPO as I would any other company's, using the same sources.
My read: huge demand for shares shows how much money still believes in AI, but sales forecasts years ahead are guesses. If Nvidia's results disappoint, that belief could cool quickly.
topics.differences: Some investors see a dominant AI company worth its price; others interviewed by Reuters question how durable its lead is and note limited disclosure.[^23][^24]
